Ps1.title: What is Communication?
Ps1.summary: An in-depth exploration of communication etymology, core definitions, transmission and understanding aspects, organizational importance, managerial functions, and communication categories.
Ps1.content:
I. What is Communication?

The word communication has been derived from the Latin word 'communis' that means ‘common’. However, communication incorporates, besides commonality, the concepts of transfer, meaning and information.

The Golden Rule: “You cannot not communicate”. This statement is quite often misunderstood by many of us; people may be fussy about the grammar of this sentence and that is at the cost of its spirit.

Core Definition: Communication can be defined as the process through which two or more persons come to exchange ideas and understanding among them.

II. Two Aspects in Communication

  • Transmission: There is something, which is transmitted, such as facts, feelings, ideas, etc. This implies that there must be a receiver if communication is to occur.
  • Understanding: The definition emphasizes the understanding element in the communication. Sharing of understanding would be possible only when the person, to whom the message is meant, understands it in the same sense in which the sender of the message wants him to understand.

III. Notable Definitions of Communication

  • T.S. Mathews: "Communication is something so simple and difficult that we can never put it in simple words".
  • Peter Little: “Communication is the process by which information is transmitted between individuals and / or organizations so that an understanding response results”.
  • W.H. Newman and C.F. Summer Jr.: “Communication is an exchange of facts, ideas, opinions, or emotions by two or more persons”.

IV. Importance of Communication

Communication is as important to the organization as blood is to the body. It serves as a medium through which:

  • Works being done in the organization can be explained.
  • Change can be affected.
  • A feeling of cooperation can be caused by establishing uniformity among the works of various people working in the organization.
  • Clear human relations can be established.
  • The objectives of the organization are realized.

Management Foundation: “Good communication is the foundation of sound management.” Its importance in management includes:

  • Basis of decision making: Much information has to be collected for decision making and for giving final shape to any idea. This information is obtained through communication.
  • Effective communication promotes spirit of cooperation and coordination: Creates an atmosphere of mutual trust and confidence between employer and employee.
  • Effective control: Managers get information about work performance through communication on the basis of which they can improve upon irregularities well in time.
  • Basis of Motivation: Helps managers in changing the point of view of the subordinates, raising their morale, and presenting a basis of satisfaction.
  • Establishment of Effective Leadership: Leadership cannot be imagined without effective communication.

V. Business Communication Categories

“Communication is the life blood of business. No business can develop in the absence of effective internal and external communication.”

  • Internal Communication (Within the Organization): Important because business has grown in size, business activity has become extremely complex, and it promotes a spirit of understanding and cooperation.
  • External Communication: Includes communication with government agencies and departments on the one hand, and distributors, retailers, individual customers, and the general public on the other.
  • Nature of Communication: The importance of communication in business becomes even more apparent when we consider an organization's communication activities from an overall perspective.

VI. The Three Categories of Communication

  • Internal - Operational Communication: Consists of structured communication within the organization that directly relates to achieving the organization's work goals.
  • External - Operational Communication: Part of an organization's structured communication concerned with achieving work goals that is conducted with people and groups outside the organization.
  • Personal Communication: All the incidental exchange of information and feelings in which human beings engage whenever they come together.

Ps2.title: Effective Communication Skills: The 7 C's
Ps2.summary: An exploration of the objectives of communication, insurmountable difficulties in measuring responses, and the detailed breakdown of the 7 C's of effective communication.
Ps2.content:
I. Objectives of Communication

Definition: The objective of communication may be defined as the passing of ideas and understanding from the sender to the target with the view to getting the desired behavioral response from the latter.

Insurmountable difficulties: Finding out the actual behavioral responses and comparing these with the expected ones, however, in case of this continuously on-going process, presents insurmountable difficulties.

II. 7 C’s of Effective Communication

The 7 C’s of communication are the principles explained to:

  • Effectively communicate so that the targeted group may understand the intended purpose.
  • Offer guidelines for individuals to learn how effectively they can influence people with their own or organizational agendas.

1. Completeness

It refers to a communication between sender and receiver when all the relevant information has been sent by the sender after analyzing the receiver’s mindset by ensuring no necessary information is missed during communication.

In case the intellectual level of the receiver demands clarification concerning the information provided; the sender should be in a position to satisfy the receiver by answering the relevant queries. This will result in effective communication with completeness of information. Otherwise, the communication will not be effective.

2. Conciseness

During interaction, the use of accurate information in short sentences will be considered as a concise way of communication.

Provisioning of concise useful information would be much regarded as effective communication while the response from the audience will also be positive.

Keywords: To the point.

3. Consideration

It refers to a communication where the advantage of the receiver is given due attention by respecting the mental perception and awareness of the receiver.

The communication mainly focuses on the needs, thoughts and requirements of the receivers with a positive approach.

Example: The interaction of political leaders with the public is mainly describing the needs and problems of the people, which are directly influencing the targeted group of people and play an emotional part in it.

Keywords: About people.

4. Concreteness

Concreteness refers to the specifics where interaction is performed with preciseness or by referring to statistics.

This creates a pronounced effect on the receivers as compared to the general talks.

5. Clarity

The endeavor for effective communication is to transfer your thoughts and ideas into the mind of the receiver.

It can effectively occur when a simple, precise and easy set of words are used for communication in order to express the purpose without going into extensive interaction.

Keywords: Simplicity.

6. Courtesy

A polite word can play a prominent role in resolving disputes among people.

Understanding the mentality of receivers of information and their feelings towards the intended interaction is very important for effective communication.

It creates a long lasting effect even if there is a difference of opinion between communicating with people or organizations.

Keywords: Respect for Audience.

7. Correctness

It refers to the factual accuracy of words used in communication between or people communicating with organizations.

It is important in both verbal and non-verbal communication where selection of correct words at the right time is important.

Keywords: Facts or Proofread.
